text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High memory churn on cont-batch workers in us-west-2. KV cache eviction rate spiked ~10x, paging observed, latency > 2s for /v1/generate and increased 5xxs on embeddings. Auto-rollbacks triggered.

alex: saw the alert. paging + eviction loop looks like some requests are producing huge sequences and filling KV pages. noticing a surge from a customer flow (large long-document condense).

mike: confirmed. tailing logs: many batches hit max_batch_tokens but also max_num_seqs per batch is high causing oversized batches that stress KV cache. UI shows continuous-batching enabled for the affected model group.

raul: stack traces show frequent KV cache page writes followed by immediate evictions -> thrash. suspect bad prompt loop from client causing long contexts.

jess: quick ask: any customer-visible errors? support dashboard shows uptick in timeouts for a handful of accounts on hosted API, mostly for endpoints hitting the longform summarization route.

kevin: digging into metrics: cont-batch queue length went from 20 -> 600 in 10m; p95 token latency jumped from 80ms -> 2.4s. paging IOPS saturated io-wait on nodes.

alex: mitigation plan: 1) throttle continuous batching for that model group 2) reduce max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 1024 3) lower max_num_seqs from 64 -> 8 4) increase KV cache eviction grace to avoid immediate thrash 5) add temporary per-customer rate limit.

priya: I'll own the throttle + config change. I'll patch runtime config via ops-console and roll to 10% of fleet, then 100% if stable.

mike: addendum: we should also disable prefix caching for that customer flow until we validate request shapes. prefix/KV caching likely exacerbates footprint.

raul: command I ran for quick relief (kubectl):
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/cont-batcher CONT_BATCHING_ENABLED=false --overwrite
```
this will stop continuous batching on a small canary set of pods.

ajess: reaction: :thumbsup:

kevin: prod-change: reduced max_batch_tokens at config layer. Patch applied to routing layer via `redwoodctl`:
```
redwoodctl config set inference.max_batch_tokens 1024 --selector=model=longform-summarize --env=prod --force
```

alex: monitoring after change — KV eviction rate dropping, paging writes down ~60% in 6m. latency p95 falling to ~500ms. some 5xxs still happening but reduced.

priya: rolling the throttle to 100% now. Also enabled per-customer throttles for the three highest-volume keys.

jess: filed a short customer-impact note: affected customers seeing timeouts between 14:12-14:27 UTC, partial failures; we should notify CSMs.

mike: note: disabling continuous batching increased CPU but reduced IO pressure. We need to monitor cost impact.

kevin: live metric snapshot: cont-batch queue length back to ~30, but KV cache size still elevated. eviction latency normalized.

raul: still seeing a few error spikes tied to requests with >1e5 tokens (malformed). I'm pushing a safety limiter to reject requests >50k tokens with 400 response.

alex: good. add to rollback playbook: if latency resurges, revert max_batch_tokens to 2048 and re-enable batching with strict seq caps, or fallback to smaller model.

priya: preparing handoff to night on-call (sre-oncall). Summary: throttled continuous batching, reduced max_batch_tokens->1024, max_num_seqs->8, disabled prefix caching for offending model group, applied per-customer rate limits, safety limiter for >50k tokens. KV eviction down, paging IOPS reduced, p95 latency improved to ~420ms. Customer note filed.

sre-oncall: acknowledged. I'll take 3-hour watch, keep alerts on 5xxs and KV eviction rate. If >2x baseline, escalate to eng-runtime.

jess: CSM FYI message drafted, will send after approval from incident lead.

mike: postmortem items to add: - add guardrails to continuous-batching configs so single request can't create >N batch tokens - surface per-customer batch footprint in console - automatic fallback to smaller model variant when KV pages exceed threshold - more granular alerts for eviction loops vs normal cache churn.

alex: agree. Also we should add a quick test to the onboarding flows to detect clients that submit huge contexts repeatedly.

priya: handing over now. handoff notes posted in ops-runbook channel. tagging @sre-oncall for link to dashboards.

sre-oncall: got it. will loop in eng-runtime if we see re-escalation. logging the incident as Sev2, creating incident ticket INC-266789 on pagerduty.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Incident INC-266789 created. Severity: S2. Summary: KV cache eviction loop due to oversized continuous-batch config + high seq loads. Current status: mitigated. Owners: priya (mitigation), sre-oncall (monitoring).

alex: thanks team. closing thread for now, will follow up with postmortem doc.

jess: :white_check_mark: will coordinate customer comms and postmortem timeline.
